data.name: Saumya
data.gender_notes: Saumya is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Saumya is derived from the Sanskrit word 'saum' meaning 'tranquil' or 'calm'. In Hindu mythology, Saumya is considered the gentle, compassionate aspect of the god of the sun, Surya. The name is often given to girls to signify kindness, graciousness, and a calming presence. The name Saumya carries the meaning “Gracious, Kind” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Saumya usually hope their child will grow to embody gracious, kind and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Saumya belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gracious, Kind.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Saumya total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

It is believed that those who bear the name Saumya possess a compassionate and gentle nature, reflecting the qualities of the deity Surya. vedic_reference.note: The name ‘Saumya’ is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘सौम्य’ (saumya), which is mentioned in various Hindu scriptures, including the Vedas and the Puranas. This word is used to describe the peaceful, calm, and soothing qualities of the divine beings, such as the gods and goddesses. The name is therefore considered to be of great spiritual significance and is often given to children as a mark of respect for the divine.
